sections.h2: Who runs a North Carolina register of deeds office, and what is it for?
sections.html:
Voters in each county elect a register of deeds every two years (G.S. 161-1). The office keeps the public land records: deeds, deeds of trust and related papers. It sits apart from the tax assessor, so a property record at one office does not update the other.

Two chores fall to the register beyond filing. It takes the statewide recording charges, and it takes the deed excise tax before a conveyance is placed on the record (G.S. 161-10). At a typical sale the closing attorney carries the new deed and the lender's deed of trust to this office.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees charged by a register of deeds?
sections.html:
The charges come from one state statute, so a deed costs the same in a mountain county as on the coast. The table repeats each charge as G.S. 161-10 prints it.

Statewide charges for common filings
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 buys the first 15 pages; each page after that adds $4.00
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 buys the first 35 pages; each page after that adds $4.00
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgageNone
Plat$21.00 for every sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 for every later page
Document that misses the format rules$25.00 on top of the usual charge
Further instrument inside one document$10.00 apiece

The statute describes these amounts as complete and exclusive, and the clerk collects them before filing. Deed excise tax is billed on top of them.

sections.h2: How does the deed excise tax work at the register of deeds counter?
sections.html:
The seller, called the transferor in the statute, hands the tax to the register before the deed is recorded. G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at $1.00 for every $500, or fraction of $500, of consideration or value.

A parcel that straddles county lines is taxed where the larger share of its value lies. Revenue is split: half stays with the county and the other half, less refunds and an allowance, moves to the Department of Revenue monthly. Gifts, inheritance transfers and deals in which the buyer owes no money or property fall outside the tax under G.S. 105-228.29.

sections.h2: What should I carry to the register of deeds?
sections.html:
Carry a deed whose signatures were acknowledged before an authorized officer. G.S. 47-14 tells the register to refuse any paper needing an acknowledgment unless one appears on it with the officer's signature, commission expiration date and seal where required.

  • The signed instrument with the notary page attached.
  • Letter-size or legal-size paper, with a blank band of three inches across the top of page one.
  • Black print on white stock at 9 points or larger, one side only.
  • The kind of instrument written at the head of the first page.
  • Money for the recording charge and any excise tax, since both are taken up front.

A paper that misses the format rules is still accepted, but it draws the nonstandard add-on from G.S. 161-14. If the only flaw is print under 9 points, the register may skip that add-on when the text is readable.

sections.h2: How fast must the register of deeds record a document?
sections.html:
Instruments go on the record in the exact order they arrive, each stamped with the day and hour it was presented. Same-day registration is the norm. If an office keeps a temporary index while it catches up, every item must reach the permanent indexes within 30 days of presentation (G.S. 161-14).

The stamp carries legal weight. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option, right of first refusal or lease longer than three years does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered, and priority tracks the order of registration by time. That is why a closing attorney records the deed the same day funds move.

sections.h2: Does a register of deeds accept electronic recording or paper copies of e-documents?
sections.html:
Electronic recording is for approved submitters only. G.S. 47-14(a1) lets a register accept an e-document from a government unit or from a trusted submitter that has signed a memorandum of understanding with that county's office. Ask the office whether your closing attorney or title company is on its list.

Paper fills the gaps. A register must record a printed copy of an electronic document when the county has no e-recording system, when the system will not take that type of document, or when the system is down. The printed copy has to carry a sworn certificate that the print is true and unaltered. The statute does not address mailed filings, so telephone the office before sending anything.

  • Ask which payment types the office takes.
  • Include the property address and a return address with a mailed deed.
  • Keep the receipt showing book, page and time of recording.

sections.h2: Can an already recorded paper be recorded again?
sections.html:
Yes, as a rerecording. The earlier instrument, or a certified copy of it, must be conspicuously marked on page one as a rerecording (G.S. 47-14(a)). People use this after a recording error has been corrected.

The office may rely on that marking and on the original recording data. It need not recheck the acknowledgment or hunt for later alterations, so have the closing attorney review a corrected deed before it is resubmitted.

A notary seal gets its own presumption. Once the register accepts a record, the law presumes a clear image of the seal was on it, and the office may not refuse a record because the seal falls short of the notary statute. A later court finding that the seal was invalid does not hurt someone who recorded an interest in the property before that finding.

sections.h2: What can I do if the register of deeds turns my document away?
sections.html:
Apply to a district court judge in the district for an order. G.S. 47-14(b) allows this when registration was denied for a missing proof or acknowledgment. The judge orders registration after finding that a signer's execution was proved or acknowledged before an authorized officer, and that the acknowledgment shows the officer's signature, commission expiration date and seal where required.

The register is not required to judge whether a paper is legally sufficient, so a recorded deed is not proof that it works. Have an attorney confirm title before you rely on the record.

faqs.q: Which county office handles a deed for my North Carolina house?
faqs.a: The register of deeds for the county that holds the land. If a parcel crosses two counties, pay the deed excise tax in the one with the larger share of the value and ask that office how to file.

faqs.q: What does a register of deeds charge for a standard deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page. Excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value can apply separately and is paid to the same office.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to file proof that a mortgage was paid off?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 lists no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

faqs.q: Why would a register of deeds refuse a deed?
faqs.a: Usually because a required acknowledgment does not appear to have been taken before an officer with authority. A district court judge can order registration if the proof or acknowledgment meets the statute.

faqs.q: How soon after I hand in a deed does it appear in the index?
faqs.a: The register is meant to record it the same day. An office using a temporary index must still finish permanent indexing within 30 days after presentation.
